correctness.rationale: For every N≥3, an exact variance perturbation excludes all non-two-level directions as local minima. All remaining normalized two-level directions are constructed explicitly. At each one, every tangent vector splits into two zero-sum blocks, and the attained sharp inequality \(1\le M(\max_U v-\min_L v)^2\) yields the exact positive local slope. A uniform coordinate-difference bound guarantees exact separation of the two blocks on the stated angular interval, so the full finite-angle envelope is established analytically. The proof handles singleton blocks and all quantifiers; a standalone checker verified 135 small finite orbits but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The nearest fully inspected works already give all complementary-face separation heights and the regular simplex global minimum, which are explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. The newly proved component is the exhaustive strict local-minimum classification with attained sharp finite-angle spherical width envelope at *every* balanced or unbalanced partition. Existing broad width-Lipschitz results control maximal absolute variation rather than the minimum positive escape slope. Actual semantic and literature searches found no equal or stronger covering claim. An inaccessible 1977 historical article and indexed full-text limits remain priority risks.

value.rationale: This fully classifies a natural nonsmooth nonconvex geometric optimization landscape: a regular simplex has exponentially many strict, mostly nonglobal, width traps. The sharp attained angular envelopes and their explicit dependence on partition imbalance give quantitative basin geometry and optimal local error-growth constants, rather than merely reprinting the known global width or partition distances. This helps understand directional-width stability and descent traps for simplex geometry.
